# R102.a synthetic .skp fixtures — provenance.

Source: OpenSKP at commit 23a15e8742e936694bf14aa029cb0e2862dce5b9
        (archive sha256 5b304cc024b2d72504ac5a6676968166fdd300f180d3f1078efe8b959951e1a5).
Fixture writer: OpenSKP's own C++ writer, packages/cpp (create.hpp), built unmodified
        from that commit; every file here is a legacy v17 container.
Deps (the pins the upstream packages/cpp/CMakeLists.txt fetches, pre-placed at the
        FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_* paths below): miniz 77d0dce8627735138c51770d1799a1ef48f2117d,
        tinygltf 488a70a3df62a4df1a736e9e56fb8836580c4888, flatbuffers v25.12.19.

Exact command (run from a checkout of this repository; the openskp tree and deps are the
pinned checkout above, e.g. $OPENSKP=/path/to/openskp@23a15e87...):

  cmake -G Ninja -B $BUILD -S $OPENSKP/packages/cpp -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DFETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_MINIZ=$DEPS/miniz \
    -DFETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_TINYGLTF=$DEPS/tinygltf \
    -DFETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_FLATBUFFERS=$DEPS/flatbuffers
  cmake --build $BUILD -j4
  g++ -std=c++17 -O2 \
    -I $OPENSKP/packages/cpp/include -I $BUILD/include \
    tests/fixtures/skp/generate.cpp $BUILD/libOpenSkp.a -o /tmp/gen_skp
  /tmp/gen_skp tests/fixtures/skp/

The generator is NOT byte-reproducible for the component fixtures (R102.b check, 2026-10-25):
the writer stamps each component definition with a random GUID (std::random_device) and a
timestamp, so a rerun changes component_instances.skp, nested_component.skp, and (R102.b)
scaled_instance.skp and mirrored_instance.skp. The other fixtures reproduce byte-for-byte on a
clean build (box, face_with_hole, hidden_tag, soft_smooth_edges and two_materials, and
textured_face). The committed bytes are the reference: rerunning the generator is not a way to
refresh them, and a changed component fixture needs its SHA below updated in the same change.

SHA-256 of the committed fixtures (tests/fixtures/skp/):
  box.skp                  05eb8f096a3b95e1a36d11c8c2c481f0f53e527579be60e1f6edeade9966c78f
  component_instances.skp  e503573d95d743604c5a1dfafab4299b2ce2dbe12af8d68c782092c56b70eb6e
  face_with_hole.skp       383bb0cdae76b6833cf9f46fdb78a9bbbd257694e0a873a9897654598258ebaa
  hidden_tag.skp           5e3c9cd202192f77929d82fc6558be4b814a034a6779fd6e2b3d03db78cc7b13
  nested_component.skp     dea7a7afcc8894e91980f75b93e53530961659d54264ca129febc96162c7fdaa
  soft_smooth_edges.skp    1a4d6c85a97431b5ad0502724328fe1e7aaf453c9beecc55e21508f9d60705fd
  two_materials.skp        a0a9a885268ef5346baa62fe2a75436e7b4a0d88b8bea8ad1db08df99f1d93c5

Contents (all coordinates in inches, as the .skp format stores them):
  box.skp                  a 1x1x1 cube, 6 faces (8 vertices, 12 edges, 6 faces)
  face_with_hole.skp       a 4x4 square with a 1x1 square hole (1 face, 1 hole)
  soft_smooth_edges.skp    two adjacent 1x0.5 faces: the lower declared soft, the upper
                           smooth (the shared edge keeps its first declaration's flags)
  two_materials.skp        two adjacent faces painted Red and Blue
  component_instances.skp  a "Widget" square, placed 3 times (the third instance hidden)
  hidden_tag.skp           a face on a layer set to hidden
  nested_component.skp     "Outer" (a 2x2 face + an instance of "Inner" at (0.5,0.5,0)),
                           placed once at the root

# R102.b additions (ADR 0176 section 4, the w question)

Three more fixtures, from the same writer and generator (tests/fixtures/skp/generate.cpp, now
run with two arguments: OUTPUT_DIR and CHECKER_PNG):

  scaled_instance.skp     a 1-inch block with outward faces (6 faces), placed with the
                          row-major 3x3 [2, 0.5, 0; 0, 1, 0; 0, 0, 1.5] (a shear and a
                          non-uniform scale) at (1, 2, 3) inches. The writer writes w = 1.
  mirrored_instance.skp   the same block, mirrored in X (3x3 diag(-1, 1, 1), determinant -1),
                          at (2, 0, 0) inches. The writer writes w = 1.
  textured_face.skp       a 4 x 4 inch face with the checker image (checker.png, 4 x 4 RGB,
                          80 bytes, committed) as a material with a 2 x 2 inch applied size, and
                          three explicit (point, (u, v)) pairs: (0,0,0)->(0,0), (4,0,0)->(1,0),
                          (0,4,0)->(0,1).

  checker.png             the image (tests/fixtures/skp/checker.png)

SHA-256 (the bytes committed; the two component fixtures are not reproducible, see above):
  scaled_instance.skp      31fb214ee14fd1410ae557d32be3a15d99f0002b0620b8a612cf928572559dac
  mirrored_instance.skp    0f121df377a264b1f43ca57b2fbecce09d6adae075f068894f87fd4b944c6718
  textured_face.skp        7767a716a1fe924782d58fd3533b48c89d3de0ad4fb1ef0131374a65f3094e9f
  checker.png              75e1a0c3dbbcab080407eb46c89cb2b2a97180f8d9bba42c527bdc7df0e82643
  named_attributes.skp     c74bf456ba1d6e030b8d12b18b468602103980e3aacd9ce3f4ac30bb29996d8b
                           (two placements of one "Chair", named "Chair A" and "Chair B"; the
                           first with a string, an integer, a float, a boolean and a Length
                           attribute; the component, so not byte-reproducible)

The w question (ADR 0176 section 4): the writer can make a scaled and a mirrored instance (the
scale and the mirror are the placement's 3x3; no separate scale is written) and always writes
w = 1, so no writer-made file has w other than 1. The import's rule (divide the translation by w,
with the scaledPlacement notice) is therefore exercised by no fixture.

# ADR 0176 follow-up, attribute reporting (2026-10-26)

  attribute_reporting.skp  10204 bytes (a legacy v17 container, from OpenSKP's writer, the same
                           command as above; the component definition gets a random GUID, so a rerun
                           changes the bytes). One definition, "Chair", with its own dictionary "Spec"
                           (String, Float, Boolean and Length: four values, none of them carried). One
                           instance, "Chair A", with a dictionary "Props" that holds a Length (not
                           carried), a 130-byte key (over the 128-byte key cap) and 130 integers named
                           Item000 to Item129 (the 128-property cap drops two of them). The writer refuses a
                           string over 255 bytes in a legacy file, so the over-2,048-byte truncation is
                           tested with an in-test package, not this file.
  SHA-256: dfca2b93434f9d18378294012abb719fbd24f692e630928cf844c59cb0fb766f
